subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency targets
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 15:10:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency targets

Alex — thanks again for the call today. Below is a quick recap and the proposed next steps so we stay aligned. Please reply with any corrections.

Summary / pain points we heard:
- P95 latency spikes during peak trading windows (they're seeing ~600–800ms p95 for text generation endpoints today).
- Streaming UX is choppy: tokens arrive in bursts and sometimes stall for 500–700ms mid-stream.
- Concurrency/throughput: baseline ~80 concurrent streams, but they see bursts to 200–250 concurrent requests for short periods.
- Cold start variability and occasional OOMs when concurrent long-context requests hit their fleet.

Current stack (as discussed):
- Self-managed inference on AWS EC2 (mixed GPU types, primarily older gen).
- Serving Llama-2 13B variants via an internal Flask + Gunicorn fronting a model process.
- Websocket-based streaming client; no prefix/KV caching in place.
- No dedicated batching layer; per-request processing.

Success criteria (what Finly said they need):
- P95 generation latency <= 250ms for typical requests (non-edge-case flows).
- Streaming token latency < 100ms to preserve smooth typing UX.
- Support baseline 80 concurrent streams with headroom to absorb spikes to 200+ with <5% error rate.
- No perceived stalls/drops during burst windows.

Suggested next steps:
1) Technical deep-dive with Aditya (SE) to share traces, exact payload sizes, and Prometheus metrics.
2) Finly to share sanitized sample traces and recent p95/P50 histograms (attachment: finly-p95-sample-trace.json).
3) Redwood to propose an initial pilot config (batching, caching, streaming buffer tuning) and a cost estimate.
4) Schedule a follow-up SLO workshop to align on monitoring and rollback policies.

Attachments: finly-infra-snapshot-20270330.pdf (infra snapshot), finly-p95-sample-trace.json (sanitized traces)

Preferred times for the deep-dive: Wed 4/2 between 09:00-11:30 PT or Thu 4/3 after 13:00 PT — what works best?

Thanks,
Marissa
Account Executive | Redwood Inference
marissa@redwood.com

From: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>

Date: Tue, 30 Mar 2027 18:05:14 -0400
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency targets

Marissa — this looks great and matches our notes. A few quick clarifications: 
- The 600–800ms p95 is for our largest workflow (customer summarization, ~1.5k tokens output). Most other flows are lower (~250–350ms p95).
- Streaming UX issues are most visible on our mobile app when clients are on flaky networks; the server-side token emission pattern seems bursty.
- Security: we'll need to run your SOC2 questionnaire and share a point of contact — security@finly.com.

We can do Wed 4/2 at 10:00 PT for the deep-dive — that works for both our infra and ML folks. I'll share the sanitized traces and a small sample of production Prometheus dashboards before the meeting.

Thanks,
Alex Johnson
Director, Product Engineering | Finly
alex.johnson@finly.com
From: Aditya Rao <aditya@redwood.com>
To: Alex Johnson <alex.johnson@finly.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Mar 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery recap: Finly - p95 latency & concurrency targets

Thanks for the recap — quick technical notes ahead of the deep-dive: 
- If possible, include request/response size distributions (tokens per request and bytes). That helps us tune batching and memory configs.
- For streaming choppiness, we'll want: per-token latency traces (server emit timestamp vs client receive) and websocket logs to determine whether the issue is server-side emission or network buffering.
- Early wins to consider: prefix/KV caching for repeated prompts, an intermediate batching layer for short requests, and tuning the streaming buffer flush interval (we can demo impact).
- Please also note any strict TLS termination or proxying in front of the model hosts (these can add jitter).

I'll prepare a short runbook we can validate in the call (deployment checklist + data we'll need). Confirming Wed 4/2 10:00 PT for the technical deep-dive — sending calendar invite now.

—Aditya
Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
aditya@redwood.com
